The manuscript gives the nonempty and empty intersection conditions and writes $\overline V\cap E_\alpha=\overline{\Sigma_\alpha^-}\cap E_\alpha$, followed by “qui est donc $\ne\varnothing$”. Its cancelled inverse-inclusion and neighbourhood argument contains the locally struck on and the replacement of formule by inserted égalité. The live restart names two closed disjoint parts Y and Z and ends with $\overline{(X\setminus(Y\cup Z))}\cap Y=\overline{(X\setminus Y)}\cap Y$, called “ce qui est immédiat” by the author. These statements remain attributed to the manuscript; no mathematical check was performed.

attributed_content_note.text: The manuscript opens with a cancelled recurrence on card K, gives intersection and nonemptiness conditions, and states an equality involving E_alpha. Its cancelled inverse-inclusion and neighbourhood argument contains the locally cancelled on and the replacement of formule by an inserted égalité. The restart names two closed disjoint parts Y and Z. The author then writes the final displayed equality and calls it « ce qui est immédiat ». These are manuscript assertions, with no proof, refutation or computation supplied by this transcription.
attributed_content_note.note: The cancelled opening proposes a recurrence on $\operatorname{card}K$; the inserted restart is “On note d’abord que”. The manuscript gives the nonempty and empty intersection conditions and writes $\overline V\cap E_\alpha=\overline{\Sigma_\alpha^-}\cap E_\alpha$, followed by “qui est donc $\ne\varnothing$”. Its cancelled inverse-inclusion and neighbourhood argument contains the locally struck on and the replacement of formule by inserted égalité. The plain V after on a and the locally qualified shared rules are retained as written. The live restart names two closed disjoint parts Y and Z and ends with $\overline{(X\setminus(Y\cup Z))}\cap Y=\overline{(X\setminus Y)}\cap Y$, called “ce qui est immédiat” by the author. These statements remain attributed to the manuscript; no mathematical check was performed.
